This pull supersedes #35743, #35746, #35750 and #35751: it carries their commits unchanged, merged onto current `main`, with one changeset in place of four. Those four pulls are closed. Merging closes all five cards.

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：照着已发布技能写应用的 AI 和开发者，现在会写对五件事：「本 ISO 周」周键占位符只能用在文本字段上；钩子和定时任务脚本编译不过会被拒收以及怎么改；初始化数据每条记录都要填识别键；运行时保存的初始化数据必须指向已存在的对象；主从子表默认就是记录页里的整宽表格。平台行为不变。
- 为什么做：属于「已发布技能文档跟上平台行为」这条线，这五条行为都已上线而技能还没写；四份改动共用同一张技能字数预算表，合成一份可避免互相排队返工。
- 出错会怎样：只改说明文字和评测样例，不动运行时；写错了 AI 会按错的说法写应用并在校验或保存时碰壁，撤回这一个合并即可恢复原文。
- 要你做什么：这是对外发布的技能文字（需人工合入的受管范围），并按既有裁决抬高了两个文件的字数上限（先删重复、余额按实测）；请在席位核对之后审批一次。

### 1. The `{current_iso_week}` period key (from #35743)

`filters.md`, section "Date Macros (declarative filter metadata)":

- A new **Period key** paragraph beside the date-macro bullets and the session tokens: `{current_iso_week}` is a member of `PERIOD_KEY_TOKENS`, not a date macro; it resolves to today's ISO week key `YYYY-Www` in the workspace time zone, Monday-start weeks, ISO week-year at year edges (2027-01-01 is `2026-W53`); it is text, for a text field storing week keys; a `date` / `datetime` / `time` field refuses it with `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 like the literal key, and the date-field spelling is `{current_week_start}` / `{current_week_end}`; a date dashboard filter's `defaultValue` and `calendar.initialDate` refuse it, a text dashboard filter may default to it; there is no last- or next-week key.
- The session-token example carries the week key on a text field (`cost_week: '{current_iso_week}'`).
- **Scope** names `resolveFilterPlaceholders()` as the client resolver, the one call over `resolveDateMacros()`, `resolvePeriodKeyTokens()` and `resolveContextTokens()`.
- The spelling check is `isKnownFilterToken(tok)`, the one predicate that answers for all three vocabularies. The two predicates the file named before both answer `false` for `current_iso_week`.

Eval 10: a text week-key field filtered with the token and a date field filtered with the week's boundaries, never with the token.

### 2. A hook or job `js` body that does not compile (from #35746)

`data-hooks.md`, section "Sandbox restrictions", gains one bullet after "Rejected by `objectstack build`":

> - **Refused when it does not compile:** a `js` source is compiled, unrun, inside its `(async (ctx) => { … })` wrapper, where `ctx` is already declared. So `const ctx = ctx.input || {};` (or `let ctx`, one name declared twice, any syntax error) is `hook-body-does-not-compile`: an **error** from `os validate`, `os build`, `os lint` and a runtime hook save (`422 INVALID_METADATA`), naming the hook, the `SyntaxError` and its line. Fix: use `ctx` as it is, or rename the local (`const input = ctx.input || {};`). A job's `js` body runs in the same wrapper: `job-body-does-not-compile`, from the three commands. A regex pattern the checking engine refuses is a warning: the runtime may accept it.

Eval case 33, at the end of the array: the refused `const ctx = …` body under `os validate`, graded on naming `hook-body-does-not-compile` and on `input.status`, a token both repairs carry and the refused source does not.

One deliberate difference from the card's wording: the card says the "save door" refuses a hook or job body. Main refuses a job body at the three commands only, because no door publishes a job (`packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts:1040`, `allowRuntimeCreate: false`; `packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts:2986`, `runtimeTypes: ['hook']`). The skill says exactly that. No published skill teaches a job `js` body anywhere else, so the job sentence lives in this one bullet.

| `422 INVALID_METADATA` at the runtime door | `packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts:1683-1684` |

### 3 and 4. Two seed refusals (from #35750)

**Keyed records (commit `b3b374b39`).** "Every record carries a value for each `externalId` field (each field of a list; `name` when the seed names none). One left blank (no value, `null` or `''`; whitespace is a value) is refused at load in every mode: the result names the object, record index, field and fix, and the other records still load." The `externalId` row of the field table points at it. Eval id 34: an `upsert` seed keyed on `code` where two records have none.

## Fold note

The five cards share one defect shape (a landed behaviour the published skill did not teach) and one fix (one paragraph and one eval case, the ratchet paid by same-file deletion first). They sit in one package, `@objectstack/skills`, with the same landing and review tier (Tier H governed surface), and all five were triaged p2. Each card keeps its own eval case as its independent check: ids 10, 33, 34, 35 and `record-page.json` case 1. Left out on purpose: #35696 and #35647, both on `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md`, which wait for #35673.

**Folded tree against the four sources.** The four heads were merged with `git merge --no-ff`, no rebase, their eight commits kept; all four merges were clean, no conflict was resolved by hand.

- Eight files are byte-identical to their one source head (same blob id): `filters.md`, `filters-pagination-search.json`, `data-hooks.md`, `seeds.md`, `relationships.md`, `objectstack-ui/evals/README.md`, `record-page.json`, `objectstack-ui/rules/record-page.md`.
- Two files have two sources each. `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`: the 35 changed lines against `origin/main` are exactly the union of the two source diffs (the `filters.md` row and the `seeds.md` row). `hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json`: the 30 added lines are the union of the two source diffs except one: case 34's `must_not_contain` is empty where #35750 wrote two tokens (contract-review should-fix S1 of record 7034102949, commit `ee231bb06`); it parses, holds 35 cases with unique ids, ids 34 and 35 after id 31 and id 33 last.
- The one difference: the four changeset files are replaced by `.changeset/35496-skills-teach-five-landed-behaviours.md`. It carries the four bodies under one title, with four bold lead-ins added. One sentence was reworded: #35751 wrote "Both rules files are shorter than before. No ceiling moves.", which is no longer true of a tree where two other rows move; it now reads "Both of those rules files are shorter than before, and neither one's token ceiling moves."

**Prior review inputs, cited and not relied on** (each was made on a source head, none on this one): contract-review records 7031292409 (#35743 at `47fe0105`) and 7031303652 (#35746 at `03b9383f`; its S1 and S2 were answered in `0c9f76eb`), and the seat ACCEPT records 7031096611 and 7031127238.

## Tests

No package source changes, so no build closure, unit test or ablation is owed. Five eval cases, one per card (above). Local readings are gates, taken at `0c80caa0b`; the one later commit, `ee231bb06`, changes one eval JSON line, and at it the token ratchet with its self-test, the skill gates, the two changeset gates and the overlap check were re-run, all exit 0. The readings are under Verification.

## Acceptance notes

Carried from the source pulls:

- Period key: the `this_week` preset the card offers as a date-field alternative is left out; where a preset is a legal filter comparand is a separate rule not measured here. The server reads the request's reference time zone (`filter-tokens.ts:172`, UTC when the request carries none); the skill says "workspace time zone", the wording of the spec's own description table. Whole-value only is true on main and not written again: the section's "Unknown tokens" paragraph already says it for every token.
- `filters.md`: the section's opening ("compute the date yourself" for ad-hoc queries) and its Scope paragraph ("use tokens in a hand-issued engine query too") pull in different directions. Older text, not changed.
- Compile refusal: the neighbouring bullet's older "Rejected by `objectstack build`" wording is left as it is.
- Seeds: the first rule is stated once, in "`externalId` selection", with a pointer from the `externalId` row; the composite-key sentence is covered by "each field of a list".
- Body table: `relationships.md` lost one true clause to pay for the new text, "owned (`master_detail`) children first" (the derived order when the parent declares no `relatedLists`, `deriveRelatedLists.ts:424-428`); the Order bullet under it still teaches the authored order.
